newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Work begins to open Hebron road to Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Work begins to open Hebron road to Palestinians.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian workers cleared roadblocks from a section of a main thoroughfare in the West Bank town of Hebron on Sunday night in preparation to opening it to Palestinian traffic on Monday, witnesses said.

They said workers from Israel's Civil Administration occupation authority and Hebron's Palestinian municipality also erected signs saying the section of road was open only to taxis and Palestinian municipal traffic.

Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO rule on January 17 under a U.S.-brokered deal. Shuhada (Martyrs) street, which borders Jewish settlements, remains in the 20 percent of the city still under Israeli control.

The accord states that the street, closed to Palestinian vehicles since February 1994 when a Jewish settler from a nearby settlement massacred 29 Arabs kneeling in prayer at al-Ibrahimi mosque, will be gradually reopened within four months.
The Palestinian vegetable market is located on Shuhada street. Some 400 Jewish settlers, who opposed the handover, live in the heart of the volatile city, home to 100,000 Arabs.
The Israeli army said on Sunday night that on Monday part of the street would be opened and that only to taxis and municipal vehicles.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had complained Israel was delaying opening the street.

Earlier on Sunday at the World Economic Forum in the Swiss town of Davos, Arafat bitterly complained Israel was breaking peace agreements, dragging its feet on solving disputes and crippling the Palestinian economy.
Shuhada street is just the tip of the iceberg.

Palestinian demands include the release of prisoners, a safe passage between Gaza and the West Bank, less restriction on the flow of people and goods between Israel and the Palestinian territories and Israeli clearance for Gaza airport to open and work to start on a Gaza seaport.
